verdict.gold_reason: Article 31(7) of Directive 2019/944 states that a DSO must procure non-frequency ancillary services via market-based procedures unless the regulatory authority has assessed that market-based provision is economically not efficient and granted a derogation. It also states that the obligation does not apply to fully integrated network components.

other_articles.why: Article 32(1) lets DSOs skip market-based procurement of flexibility services if the regulator finds it economically inefficient or likely to cause severe market distortions or higher congestion. It covers flexibility services, not non-frequency ancillary services as such, and has no fully-integrated-components exception.

verdict.ambiguity_reason: 'Local grid company' maps to the DSO and 'grid-support products with nothing to do with frequency' to non-frequency ancillary services. Article 32 on flexibility services is a loosely related exception, but the wording points to Article 31(7).
